metadata.purpose: Verified source-backed rule pack for a future cap-table, dilution, SAFE, convertible note, option pool, anti-dilution, Israel/Delaware, and founder benchmark skill. v0.3.1: added `safe.pre_money_cap_conversion` rule for legacy YC pre-money SAFE forms (yc_premoney_cap_only, pre_money_cap_and_discount_legacy). Post-J audit surfaced that the math producer applied the post-money formula universally; pre-money SAFEs must use pre-financing FD as denominator (cap_price = cap / pre_money_FD). The new rule documents the formula + the multi-SAFE denominator ambiguity (pre-existing snapshot vs as-converted interpretation; v0.1 uses pre-existing). Math producers' `RULE_PACK_VERSION` constants bumped 0.3.0 → 0.3.1. v0.3.0: clarified `safe.post_money_cap_conversion` denominator semantics. For YC post-money SAFEs, the ownership identity `safe_ownership = purchase / post_money_cap` is the load-bearing rule (per `safe.stacked_post_money_caps` and YC-PMSAFE-PRIMER worked examples). The downstream restatement `safe_price = cap / company_capitalization` must use a denominator that satisfies this identity — which is the FULL post-money fully-diluted snapshot INCLUDING new-money shares, not the pre-financing snapshot. Producers that pass pre-financing FD as `company_capitalization` produce the pre-money YC SAFE formula and under-allocate SAFE shares (math bug fixed in cap-table priced_round.py at this version). Earlier v0.2.x history below. v0.2.2: added NVCA-CERT-OF-INC and COOLEY-DOWN-ROUND as proper source IDs for the BBWA rule (formerly the rule cited NVCA Model Cert in prose without a corresponding source_id; the formula text is in the Cooley down-round article, not the glossary). v0.2.1 history: reverted BBWA B-divisor to CP1; replaced WSGR Q1 figures with verified FY2025 medians; softened ICNL Ordinance caveat. v0.2.0 history: TaxAdviser QSBS URL fix; ICNL Companies Law canonical PDF; WSGR direct URL; qualified-financing benchmark rewrite; Section 102 double-trigger split; option-pool source list cleaned; YC primer co-cites added. v0.2.3: appended verbatim BBWA formula text + 2022-01-24 last-reviewed date from Cooley GO down-round article into the COOLEY-DOWN-ROUND source notes; tightened COOLEY-ANTI-DILUTION notes to flag it as the concept-level glossary corroborator (formula text lives on COOLEY-DOWN-ROUND). v0.2.4: swapped NVCA-CERT-OF-INC URL from the index landing page to the direct downloadable .docx; verified §4.4.4 contains the verbatim CP1-based BBWA formula text by extracting the document XML. v0.2.5: schema documents counsel_review semantics (reliance boundary, not confidence score) and adds optional script_allowed_outputs / script_disallowed_outputs enums; markdown gains a Counsel Review Semantics section. v0.2.6: schema adds optional `date_window.near_edge_days_before_start` and `date_window.near_edge_days_before_end` override fields per cap-table skill design (rev3); rule defaults remain 30/90 days; no rules in v0.2.6 use the overrides yet, but the schema permits them.

safe.title: Post-money SAFE cap conversion
safe.summary: For a post-money SAFE with a valuation cap, the cap-implied ownership equals the SAFE purchase amount divided by the post-money valuation cap; conversion shares are purchase amount divided by the applicable conversion price.
safe.applies_when: Use for YC post-money SAFE valuation-cap forms, subject to the document's Company Capitalization definition and conversion branch.

inputs.name: purchase_amount
inputs.description: Cash invested under the SAFE.

inputs.name: post_money_valuation_cap
inputs.description: Post-money valuation cap in the SAFE.

inputs.name: company_capitalization
inputs.description: Document-defined fully diluted capitalization denominator.

inputs.name: equity_financing_price
inputs.description: Cash price per share paid by new money investors in the equity financing.

inputs.name: discount_multiplier
inputs.description: Discount multiplier when the SAFE includes a discount branch, such as 0.8 for a 20 percent discount.

outputs.name: cap_implied_ownership
outputs.description: Purchase amount divided by post-money valuation cap.

outputs.name: safe_price
outputs.description: Post-money valuation cap divided by Company Capitalization.

outputs.name: conversion_price
outputs.description: Lowest valid conversion price under the document's cap, discount, or other conversion branch.

outputs.name: safe_shares
outputs.description: Purchase amount divided by conversion price before document-defined share rounding.

safe.rounding_policy: Keep internal calculations at decimal precision. Apply only the SAFE document's fractional-share or cash-in-lieu rule at issuance.
warnings: Do not reuse pre-money SAFE denominator logic for a post-money SAFE.

The load-bearing identity is `safe_ownership_i = purchase_amount_i / post_money_valuation_cap_i` (per `safe.stacked_post_money_caps` and YC primer worked examples). When implementing `safe_shares = purchase / (cap / company_capitalization)`, the `company_capitalization` denominator must equal the full post-money fully-diluted snapshot including new-money shares so that `safe_shares = ownership × post_money_FD` collapses to the identity. Passing the pre-financing FD as `company_capitalization` (the pre-money SAFE denominator) under-allocates SAFE shares and over-states founder ownership — common implementation bug. Solver implementations should iterate `company_capitalization` toward the converged post-money FD.

safe.title: YC post-money SAFE Company Capitalization denominator
safe.summary: YC post-money SAFE conversion math depends on the document-defined Company Capitalization denominator, including existing shares, promised options, available option pool, and converting securities, while excluding new-money financing shares and most new pool increases.
safe.applies_when: Use when the selected form is the YC post-money SAFE or a derivative using the same Company Capitalization definition.

inputs.name: pre_financing_common_equivalents
inputs.description: All common and preferred stock on an as-converted basis before the financing.

inputs.name: promised_options
inputs.description: Shares promised under options or similar rights.

inputs.name: unissued_option_pool
inputs.description: Shares available for future grant under the stock plan before the financing.

inputs.name: converting_securities
inputs.description: Shares issuable on conversion of all SAFEs and other convertible securities, before new-money preferred shares.

outputs.name: company_capitalization
outputs.description: Document-defined denominator used for safe price.

warnings: Flag any model that includes the new-money financing shares in this denominator.
Flag any model that includes a new post-financing pool increase unless the SAFE's promised-options overflow rule applies.

safe.title: SAFE discount multiplier semantics
safe.summary: YC SAFE forms express discount math through a Discount Rate multiplier defined in the SAFE template's Definitions section, so a 20 percent discount is modeled as 80 percent of the priced-round price, not as 20 percent of it.
safe.applies_when: Use for SAFE documents using the YC-style Discount Rate definition.

inputs.name: priced_round_price
inputs.description: Price paid by new-money investors in the equity financing.

inputs.name: discount_multiplier
inputs.description: Document-defined multiplier, such as 0.8.

outputs.name: discount_price
outputs.description: Priced-round price multiplied by the discount multiplier.

warnings: Warn when user-entered discount exceeds 1.0 but appears intended as a percentage, such as 20 instead of 0.8.

safe.title: Pre-money (legacy) SAFE cap conversion
safe.summary: For a YC pre-money SAFE (legacy form, used by YC pre-Oct-2018) with a valuation cap, the conversion price equals the pre-money valuation cap divided by the PRE-FINANCING fully-diluted snapshot. Unlike post-money SAFEs, the SAFE's percentage of post-money is NOT fixed at purchase/cap; the SAFE dilutes alongside founders when new money and any pool refresh land.
safe.applies_when: Use for YC pre-money SAFE valuation-cap forms (yc_premoney_cap_only and pre_money_cap_and_discount_legacy). These SAFEs were the YC default from May 2014 to October 2018; they continue to appear on cap tables of older companies.

inputs.name: purchase_amount
inputs.description: Cash invested under the SAFE.

inputs.name: pre_money_valuation_cap
inputs.description: Pre-money valuation cap in the legacy SAFE.

inputs.name: pre_money_fully_diluted_shares
inputs.description: Pre-financing fully-diluted snapshot: founders + issued preferred (as-converted) + outstanding options + unissued option pool, BEFORE the SAFE itself converts and BEFORE new money and any pool refresh.

inputs.name: discount_multiplier
inputs.description: Discount multiplier when the SAFE includes a discount branch, such as 0.8 for a 20 percent discount. Required for pre_money_cap_and_discount_legacy.

inputs.name: equity_financing_price
inputs.description: Cash price per share paid by new money investors in the equity financing. Required for the discount candidate.

outputs.name: safe_price
outputs.description: Pre-money valuation cap divided by pre-financing fully-diluted shares.

outputs.name: conversion_price
outputs.description: Lowest valid conversion price under the document's cap (or cap-and-discount) branch.

outputs.name: safe_shares
outputs.description: Purchase amount divided by conversion price, before document-defined share rounding.

safe.rounding_policy: Keep internal calculations at decimal precision. Apply only the SAFE document's fractional-share or cash-in-lieu rule at issuance.
parameterization_points: pre_money_fully_diluted_shares definition (whether multiple converting SAFEs are included on an as-converted basis is document-specific; v0.1 uses pre-existing snapshot interpretation)
warnings: Do not reuse post-money SAFE denominator logic for a pre-money SAFE. Post-money SAFEs lock `purchase/cap` of post-money FD; pre-money SAFEs lock `purchase/cap` of PRE-money FD and dilute downstream from new money / pool refresh.

Multi-SAFE pre-money scenarios with simultaneous conversion have a known ambiguity in the YC primer: each SAFE's denominator may or may not include the OTHER converting SAFEs on an as-converted basis. v0.1 uses the pre-existing-snapshot interpretation (each SAFE prices off the same pre-financing FD). Counsel may need to confirm against the actual SAFE document language for scenarios with 2+ pre-money SAFEs.

Pre-money SAFEs are friendlier to founders, less friendly to early investors than post-money SAFEs (which is why YC changed the default in October 2018). Confirm form classification when extracting from documents pre-dating that switch.

safe.title: Stacked post-money SAFE ownership
safe.summary: Multiple post-money SAFEs each reserve a fixed post-conversion ownership percentage before the next equity round; the total SAFE ownership is the sum of purchase amount divided by post-money cap for each SAFE, subject to feasibility checks.
safe.applies_when: Use when multiple post-money valuation-cap SAFEs convert in the same equity financing.

inputs.name: pre_safe_fully_diluted_shares
inputs.description: Fully diluted shares before SAFE conversion and before new-money financing shares.

inputs.name: safes
inputs.description: SAFE entries with purchase amount and post-money valuation cap.

outputs.name: safe_ownership_percentages
outputs.description: Ownership percentage for each SAFE.

outputs.name: aggregate_safe_ownership
outputs.description: Sum of SAFE ownership percentages.

outputs.name: post_safe_pre_money_shares
outputs.description: Implied shares after SAFE conversion and before new-money financing shares.

safe.rounding_policy: Calculate ownership and implied shares at high precision; apply document-defined share rounding after each SAFE's share issuance calculation.
parameterization_points: whether all SAFEs use post-money caps
treatment of uncapped or discount-only SAFEs
warnings: Block or escalate when aggregate SAFE ownership is greater than or equal to 100 percent.
Warn when stacked post-money SAFEs leave implausibly low founder or employee ownership.

safe.title: MFN election is document-specific and package-based
safe.summary: YC MFN SAFE terms are elected by accepting the later instrument package as a whole, rather than selectively cherry-picking individual favorable terms.
safe.applies_when: Use for YC MFN SAFE forms and YC standard-deal MFN analysis.
warnings: Do not model MFN as automatic cherry-picking unless the actual signed document says so.
Prompt for the signed document text when a user says an MFN SAFE converts automatically.

safe.title: Pro rata rights are separate and capped by document
safe.summary: YC pro rata rights are granted through a separate side letter, not automatically by every SAFE; ownership and future purchase rights are capped by the applicable side-letter terms.
safe.applies_when: Use when modeling post-financing ownership after investor pro rata participation.
warnings: Do not assume pro rata rights exist from a SAFE alone.
Prompt for whether the pro rata side letter was signed and whether it applies only to a Major Investor.

safe.title: SAFE liquidity and dissolution priority
safe.summary: SAFE treatment in liquidity and dissolution events is a separate document-defined branch (post-money SAFE Sections 1(c) and 1(d)) and should not be collapsed into equity-round conversion math. Liquidity: greater of purchase amount or as-converted proceeds. Dissolution: return of purchase amount.
safe.applies_when: Use when a scenario includes sale, IPO, dissolution, or shutdown before an equity financing.
warnings: Warn that liquidity/dissolution outcomes require document branch analysis and may differ from financing conversion math.

safe.title: Israel 2025 SAFE temporary guidance
safe.summary: English law-firm summaries report that the January 2025 ITA SAFE guidance applies to qualifying Israeli-company SAFEs during 2025-2026 and uses quantitative conditions such as investment caps, ownership limits, minimum discounts, and conversion timing constraints.
safe.applies_when: Use only as a preliminary checklist for Israeli-company SAFEs; require Israeli tax counsel before tax classification, reporting, or withholding conclusions.

date_window.notes: Temporary ITA guidance period as summarized by law firms.

warnings: Counsel review required before treating a SAFE as equity-like for Israeli tax purposes.
Flag non-Israeli issuer, debt-like terms, interest, repayment rights, side payments, or investor control rights.
safe.notes: Rule should be implemented as a checklist with source-specific thresholds, not as an automatic tax classification.

safe.title: Non-qualifying Israeli SAFE facts-and-circumstances review
safe.summary: If a SAFE does not satisfy the reported 2025 ITA guidance conditions, the instrument remains facts-and-circumstances dependent and may be treated as debt, equity, or another instrument for tax purposes.
safe.applies_when: Use when any reported Israeli SAFE safe-harbor condition is missing, unclear, or breached.

date_window.notes: Temporary guidance period; check for later ITA updates.

warnings: Escalate to Israeli tax counsel before modeling tax, withholding, or financial-statement treatment.

convertible_notes.title: Convertible note accrued interest
convertible_notes.summary: Convertible note conversion usually uses principal plus accrued interest unless the signed note says otherwise; interest can be simple or compounding depending on the document.
convertible_notes.applies_when: Use when a convertible note balance is converted, repaid, or modeled at maturity.

inputs.name: principal
inputs.description: Original principal amount.

inputs.name: annual_interest_rate
inputs.description: Annual interest rate as a decimal.

inputs.name: days_elapsed
inputs.description: Days from issuance or last interest event to conversion or repayment.

inputs.name: day_count_basis
inputs.description: Document-defined day count basis, usually 365 or 360.

inputs.name: compounding_periods_per_year
inputs.description: Compounding periods per year; zero or null means simple interest.

outputs.name: accrued_interest
outputs.description: Interest accrued through conversion or repayment date.

outputs.name: conversion_balance
outputs.description: Principal plus accrued interest if the document converts interest.

formula: compound_balance = principal * (1 + annual_interest_rate / compounding_periods_per_year) ^ (compounding_periods_per_year * days_elapsed / day_count_basis)
accrued_interest = simple_interest or compound_balance - principal, based on note terms
conversion_balance = principal + accrued_interest when interest converts
convertible_notes.rounding_policy: Calculate money to at least cents internally; apply document-specific rounding only at payment or share issuance.

convertible_notes.title: Convertible note cap and discount conversion
convertible_notes.summary: Convertible notes commonly convert principal plus eligible accrued interest at the lower of a valuation-cap price and a discount price, subject to the signed note's definitions.
convertible_notes.applies_when: Use when a note converts via valuation cap, discount, or both. The rule supports three sub-paths: (a) cap-only — `valuation_cap` and `capitalization_denominator` non-null, `discount_multiplier` null; (b) discount-only — `valuation_cap` and `capitalization_denominator` null, `discount_multiplier` non-null; (c) cap-and-discount — all three non-null, conversion_price = min(cap_price, discount_price). Allowed null inputs reflect which sub-path is active; per-input `required` flags are sub-path-dependent.

inputs.name: conversion_balance
inputs.description: Principal plus any eligible accrued interest.

inputs.name: valuation_cap
inputs.description: Note valuation cap.

inputs.name: capitalization_denominator
inputs.description: Document-defined denominator for cap price. Required when valuation_cap is non-null (the cap branch needs both to compute cap_price = valuation_cap / capitalization_denominator). Allowed null in the discount-only path (where valuation_cap is also null and only the discount branch fires).

inputs.name: qualified_financing_price
inputs.description: Price per share in the qualified financing. Required when the rule is invoked in the priced-round or direct-price branch; allowed null only in the maturity convert_at_cap branch (where cap_price alone is the conversion price and discount_price is not computed).

inputs.name: discount_multiplier
inputs.description: Discount multiplier, such as 0.8 for a 20 percent discount.

outputs.name: cap_price
outputs.description: Valuation cap divided by document-defined capitalization denominator.

outputs.name: discount_price
outputs.description: Qualified financing price multiplied by discount multiplier.

outputs.name: conversion_price
outputs.description: Lowest valid conversion price under the signed note.

outputs.name: conversion_shares
outputs.description: Conversion balance divided by conversion price.

convertible_notes.rounding_policy: Keep conversion price and share calculations at high precision; apply the note's fractional-share rule at issuance.

convertible_notes.title: Convertible note cap denominator is template-specific
convertible_notes.summary: Convertible note cap-price denominators vary by template and signed document; some exclude the converting note and unallocated pool, while others include different equity plan components.
convertible_notes.applies_when: Use whenever a note cap price is calculated.
warnings: Do not assume the note itself is included in its own cap denominator.
Prompt for signed note definitions when cap denominator treatment is unknown.
convertible_notes.notes: Rule scripts should support multiple named denominator policies rather than a single universal convention.

convertible_notes.title: Qualified financing threshold and automatic conversion
convertible_notes.summary: A convertible note's automatic conversion trigger is document-defined and tied to a qualified financing dollar floor. Standard US templates differ on the default (Fenwick seed: $1,000,000; NVCA Toptal: $2,000,000); WSGR FY2025 benchmark data shows observed median thresholds running materially higher than template defaults and trending up year over year.
convertible_notes.applies_when: Use when a financing round may trigger automatic note conversion.

date_window.notes: WSGR Entrepreneurs Report benchmarks reflect deals closing in 2025. Refresh annually.

benchmark.dataset: Wilson Sonsini Entrepreneurs Report Full-Year 2025 (Q4 2025 cumulative)
observations: Auto-conversion on qualified financing is near-universal across reporting cells in the Convertible Notes deal-terms appendix.
WSGR FY2025 median dollar thresholds for a qualified financing in convertible notes: $10,000,000 (pre-Seed) and $15,000,000 (post-Seed).
Standard template defaults remain: Fenwick seed-stage form $1,000,000; NVCA Toptal model $2,000,000.
benchmark.notes: Template defaults and observed market medians diverge by an order of magnitude. Use template default as a starting parameter; check the signed note for the actual trigger; observed medians refresh annually.

warnings: Warn when a model automatically converts notes without checking the note's qualified financing threshold.
Do not hardcode any single dollar figure as a legal trigger; the signed note's definition controls.

Benchmark medians refresh annually. The FY 2025 median doubled vs 2024 for pre-Seed ($5M to $10M) and rose 50 percent for post-Seed ($10M to $15M); do not treat the FY 2025 figures as durable into future years without refresh.

convertible_notes.title: Israeli convertible loan agreement tax treatment
convertible_notes.summary: Israeli convertible loan agreements can raise deemed-interest, withholding, and classification issues under Israeli tax rules; 3(i), 3(j), or other regimes may apply depending on holder and instrument facts.
convertible_notes.applies_when: Use when an Israeli company or Israeli holder has a convertible loan or note.
warnings: Escalate to Israeli tax counsel for interest accrual, withholding, and holder-specific classification.
Do not treat Israeli convertible loans as equivalent to US SAFEs.

option_pool.title: Pre-money option pool top-up
option_pool.summary: When investors require a target option pool included in the pre-money valuation, the top-up dilutes pre-financing holders because the pool increase is added before pricing new-money shares.
option_pool.applies_when: Use when the term sheet requires a post-closing pool target to be reflected in pre-money capitalization.

inputs.name: pre_topup_fully_diluted_shares
inputs.description: Fully diluted shares before the pool increase and new-money shares.

inputs.name: existing_unallocated_pool
inputs.description: Unallocated shares already in the equity incentive pool.

inputs.name: target_pool_percent
inputs.description: Target pool percentage after the financing or before the financing, depending on the term sheet.

inputs.name: new_money_shares
inputs.description: Shares issued to new-money investors if the target is post-closing.

inputs.name: target_basis
inputs.description: Denominator basis for target pool.

outputs.name: required_pool_topup_shares
outputs.description: Additional option pool shares required.

outputs.name: post_topup_pool_percent
outputs.description: Resulting pool percentage on the selected denominator.

formula: For post-money target: (existing_unallocated_pool + x) / (pre_topup_fully_diluted_shares + x + new_money_shares) = target_pool_percent
For pre-money target: (existing_unallocated_pool + x) / (pre_topup_fully_diluted_shares + x) = target_pool_percent
option_pool.rounding_policy: Solve using decimal precision; round pool share authorization to whole shares using corporate-document requirements.
parameterization_points: whether promised grants count against the target
whether converting securities count in the denominator
authorized versus reserved versus available pool distinction
warnings: Warn when a term sheet labels the pool as post-closing but shifts the economics into pre-money pricing.

option_pool.title: Post-money option pool increase
option_pool.summary: If an option pool increase is economically post-money, dilution is shared by all post-financing holders according to the selected denominator rather than solely by pre-financing holders.
option_pool.applies_when: Use when transaction documents explicitly make the pool increase post-money or after pricing.

inputs.name: post_financing_shares_before_topup
inputs.description: Shares outstanding after the financing but before the pool top-up.

inputs.name: existing_unallocated_pool
inputs.description: Unallocated pool before top-up.

inputs.name: target_pool_percent
inputs.description: Target pool percentage after top-up.

outputs.name: required_pool_topup_shares
outputs.description: Additional shares required in the pool.

option_pool.rounding_policy: Solve using decimal precision; round to whole shares under corporate-document requirements.
parameterization_points: timing of board and stockholder approvals

option_pool.title: Option pool target basis must be explicit
option_pool.summary: Option pool percentages are not meaningful unless the numerator and denominator are stated, including whether the target uses total reserved, unallocated only, promised grants, converting securities, and new-money shares.
option_pool.applies_when: Use whenever user enters an option pool percentage.
warnings: Prompt for total-reserved versus unallocated-pool target.
Warn when promised but ungranted hires are excluded from a pre-money pool target.

option_pool.title: US option pool market benchmarks
option_pool.summary: US venture-stage option pools are market benchmarks, not legal rules; common planning ranges around seed and Series A should be configurable and surfaced as context only.
warnings: Do not mark a pool size as wrong solely because it sits outside the benchmark range.

anti_dilution.title: Broad-based weighted-average anti-dilution
anti_dilution.summary: Broad-based weighted-average anti-dilution adjusts a preferred conversion price by multiplying the prior conversion price (CP1) by (A + B) divided by (A + C). The formula and B's divisor (CP1 itself) appear verbatim in NVCA Model Certificate of Incorporation Subsection 4.4.4 and Cooley GO's down-round article. The series' Original Issue Price (OIP) enters separately as the trigger threshold and any conversion-price floor, not as the divisor in B.
anti_dilution.applies_when: Use when preferred stock includes broad-based weighted-average anti-dilution protection and a down round occurs.

inputs.name: old_conversion_price
inputs.description: Preferred stock conversion price (CP1) in effect immediately before the dilutive issuance.

inputs.name: original_issue_price
inputs.description: Original issue price (OIP) of the protected preferred series; used as the trigger threshold and as any conversion-price floor. Not used as the divisor in B.

inputs.name: a_outstanding_shares
inputs.description: Document-defined outstanding shares before the dilutive issuance; for broad-based, typically includes common, preferred as-converted, options, warrants, and convertibles.

inputs.name: consideration_received
inputs.description: Total consideration received in the dilutive issuance.

inputs.name: new_shares_issued
inputs.description: Actual shares issued in the dilutive issuance.

outputs.name: b_deemed_shares
outputs.description: Consideration received divided by the prior conversion price CP1.

outputs.name: new_conversion_price
outputs.description: Adjusted conversion price (CP2) after weighted-average protection.

anti_dilution.rounding_policy: Use document-defined rounding for conversion price and conversion ratio; keep internal calculations at high precision.
parameterization_points: treatment of options, warrants, and convertible securities
trigger-threshold floor (typically OIP, sometimes CP1) defined by the charter
warnings: Do not assume all issuances trigger anti-dilution; check excluded-issuance provisions.

Stacked anti-dilution: chained ratchets feed each round's new CP back in as the next round's CP1. Do not substitute OIP for CP1 in B; that would over-credit the holder by re-counting dilution already absorbed by a prior ratchet.
anti_dilution.notes: Formula text and B-divisor (CP1) verified verbatim against Cooley GO down-round article (Last reviewed 2022-01-24) and NVCA Model Certificate of Incorporation Subsection 4.4.4. Both sources agree: B = consideration_received / CP1, where CP1 is the conversion price in effect immediately prior to the dilutive issuance.

anti_dilution.title: Narrow-based weighted-average denominator is document-defined
anti_dilution.summary: Narrow-based weighted-average formulas use a narrower share denominator than broad-based formulas; the exact denominator must come from the charter or financing documents.
anti_dilution.applies_when: Use when documents say narrow-based weighted average or define a custom anti-dilution denominator.
warnings: Prompt for the anti-dilution provision text when the denominator is not explicit.

anti_dilution.title: Full-ratchet anti-dilution
anti_dilution.summary: Full-ratchet anti-dilution resets the protected preferred conversion price to the lower new-issuance price, which is economically more punitive than weighted-average protection.
anti_dilution.applies_when: Use when preferred stock documents include full-ratchet protection.

inputs.name: new_issuance_price
inputs.description: Price per share in the dilutive issuance.

outputs.name: new_conversion_price
outputs.description: New conversion price under full ratchet.

anti_dilution.rounding_policy: Use document-defined conversion-price precision and rounding.
warnings: Flag full-ratchet protection as a high-impact investor-protection term.

israel_equity_tax.title: Section 102 capital-gains track checklist
israel_equity_tax.summary: Israeli Section 102 capital-gains treatment depends on trustee deposit, timing, employee status, approved plan mechanics, and holding-period requirements; secondary guidance should be used only as a checklist.
israel_equity_tax.applies_when: Use when modeling options, RSUs, or shares issued to Israeli employees, officers, or directors.

date_window.notes: Track plan filing, grant deposit, and required holding-period dates from the actual plan, trustee confirmations, and current ITA guidance.

warnings: Require counsel review before concluding capital-gains treatment.
Flag missing trustee deposit date, missing plan approval, or sale before required holding period.

israel_equity_tax.title: Section 102 plan-design pitfalls
israel_equity_tax.summary: Plan terms such as share class, voting rights, cash settlement, exit-only rights, repurchase arrangements, and transaction-adjacent grants can affect Israeli tax analysis. Section 102 trustee track is administratively limited to ordinary voting shares; preferred or non-voting shares typically require an ITA pre-ruling.
israel_equity_tax.applies_when: Use when checking Israeli equity plans or transaction-related option acceleration.

date_window.notes: Check current ITA guidance and circulars as of the grant, acceleration, exit, or IPO date. Pearl Cohen flags a roughly 90-day-before-LOI cutoff that the ITA uses to disqualify transaction-adjacent grants.

warnings: Escalate cash-settled rights, exit-only economics, repricing/modification of outstanding grants, transaction-adjacent grants near a signed LOI, and non-ordinary-voting-share grants to Israeli tax counsel.
Do not characterize double-trigger acceleration as inherently disqualifying without checking the current ITA position; see rule israel_equity_tax.section_102_double_trigger.

israel_equity_tax.title: Section 102 double-trigger acceleration treatment
israel_equity_tax.summary: Israeli law-firm guidance reports that under ITA Position Paper 01/2025, double-trigger acceleration of Section 102 awards on exit or IPO is not treated as a violation of Section 102. The resulting tax characterization on exit still depends on facts (cash vs equity consideration, post-closing share price movement).
israel_equity_tax.applies_when: Use when an Israeli equity plan or grant includes single- or double-trigger acceleration on change of control or IPO.

date_window.notes: ITA Position Paper 01/2025 is the current secondary-source-reported position; verify against current ITA materials at deal time.

warnings: Treat acceleration tax characterization as facts-and-circumstances; do not assert capital-gains versus ordinary-income treatment from cap-table data alone.
Pearl Cohen pre-2025 guidance treated double-trigger as severance-like and disqualifying; Shibolet reports the 2025 ITA position relaxed this. Confirm the current position with Israeli tax counsel.

israel_equity_tax.title: Section 3(i) nonemployee equity
israel_equity_tax.summary: Israeli equity or option grants to consultants, service providers, controlling shareholders, or other non-Section 102 recipients may fall outside Section 102 and require separate tax treatment.
israel_equity_tax.applies_when: Use when recipient is not an eligible employee, officer, or director under Section 102, or may be a controlling shareholder.

date_window.notes: Check recipient status and applicable law at grant and exercise/sale dates.

warnings: Do not apply Section 102 capital-gains assumptions to consultants or controlling shareholders without legal review.

israeli_ltd.title: Israeli private company share register
israeli_ltd.summary: An Israeli private company must maintain a shareholder register and the cap-table model should separate internal share-register truth from reportable filings.
israeli_ltd.applies_when: Use for Israeli private limited companies.
warnings: Require counsel or corporate secretary review before treating the model as a statutory register.

israeli_ltd.title: Israeli Registrar online reporting
israeli_ltd.summary: Law-firm guidance reports that from June 27, 2024, most filings with the Israeli Registrar of Companies must be submitted online; the cap-table skill should flag filing workflow rather than attempt filings.
israeli_ltd.applies_when: Use when Israeli share issuances, transfers, director changes, or annual-report workflows are discussed.

date_window.notes: Use current Registrar rules and Hebrew official materials before operational filing guidance.

warnings: Flag that filings are outside the cap-table calculator and require authorized Israeli corporate filing workflow.

israeli_ltd.title: Israel Innovation Authority royalties and IP restrictions
israeli_ltd.summary: IIA grants can create royalty obligations and restrictions or approvals for IP transfer, licensing, and manufacturing outside Israel.
israeli_ltd.applies_when: Use when an Israeli company received IIA support or has technology developed with IIA funding.
warnings: Escalate any investment, acquisition, flip, IP transfer, license, or manufacturing move involving IIA-funded technology.
Do not model IIA exposure as simple cap-table dilution.

israeli_ltd.title: Israeli preferred-share governance is document-specific
israeli_ltd.summary: Israeli investment rounds may include preferred-share, veto, board, protective-provision, and founder-restriction terms; the cap-table skill should capture these as term-sheet flags rather than universal formulas.
israeli_ltd.applies_when: Use when Israeli preferred shares, board rights, veto rights, liquidation preferences, or founder restrictions are modeled.
warnings: Prompt for articles, shareholder agreement, and investment agreement before modeling governance economics.

delaware_cross_border.title: Delaware parent with Israeli subsidiary is a common cross-border structure
delaware_cross_border.summary: A Delaware parent with an Israeli operating or R&D subsidiary is common for US venture-backed Israeli-linked startups, but structure choice is tax, IP, investor, and employment dependent.
delaware_cross_border.applies_when: Use when founders ask whether to model a Delaware parent, Israeli parent, or flip.
warnings: Escalate structure choice to US and Israeli tax counsel before implementing equity, IP, or payroll assumptions.

delaware_cross_border.title: Section 102 treatment for foreign parent shares
delaware_cross_border.summary: Israeli Section 102 treatment can involve foreign-parent shares, trustee mechanics, sub-plan design, and eligibility conditions; scripts should flag missing trustee and plan facts.
delaware_cross_border.applies_when: Use when Israeli employees receive Delaware-parent options or shares.

date_window.notes: Check Section 102 plan, trustee approval, and current ITA practice as of grant and sale dates.

warnings: Do not assume Delaware-parent grants are Section 102 compliant without local sub-plan and trustee confirmation.

delaware_cross_border.title: Cross-border IP and transfer pricing
delaware_cross_border.summary: Israeli R&D center and IP ownership choices can affect transfer-pricing, valuation, and exit tax outcomes; recent Israeli guidance makes this date-sensitive.
delaware_cross_border.applies_when: Use when modeling IP ownership, R&D subsidiary economics, cost-plus arrangements, or related-party services.

date_window.notes: Approximate publication month for reported final guidance; verify current ITA text before implementation.

warnings: Escalate IP migration, cost-plus rates, and related-party agreements to cross-border tax counsel.

delaware_cross_border.title: Delaware formation share defaults are configurable
delaware_cross_border.summary: Common startup formation defaults such as 10 million authorized shares and low par value are market conventions, not immutable legal requirements.
delaware_cross_border.applies_when: Use when creating initial founder cap table assumptions for a Delaware C corporation.
warnings: Do not treat formation defaults as required; prompt for actual charter values.

delaware_cross_border.title: QSBS rules are date-sensitive
delaware_cross_border.summary: US QSBS eligibility and exclusion amounts are date-sensitive and changed for stock issued after July 4, 2025 under OBBBA; cap-table scripts should flag issue date and tax counsel review.
delaware_cross_border.applies_when: Use when US C corporation shares may be QSBS or founder/investor tax outcomes depend on QSBS.

date_window.notes: OBBBA §70431 applies to stock acquired AFTER July 4, 2025 (the enactment date). The schema treats `start` as inclusive (event_date >= start), so the first in-window day is 2025-07-05. Verify current Code and guidance before applying.

warnings: Do not provide QSBS eligibility conclusion from cap-table data alone.
Prompt for issue date, gross assets, active business, entity type, redemptions, and holder facts.

delaware_flip.title: Flip mechanics require holder-by-holder mapping
delaware_flip.summary: A Delaware flip usually requires mapping Israeli company holders into Delaware parent securities through share exchange or contribution mechanics, preserving economic rights only if the legal steps and consents support it.
delaware_flip.applies_when: Use when modeling a flip from Israeli parent to Delaware parent.
warnings: Do not assume 1:1 exchange preserves all tax, option, liquidation, and consent consequences.
Prompt for articles, option plan, SAFE/note consents, IIA history, and tax ruling path.

delaware_flip.title: Israeli flip ruling path is not one-size-fits-all
delaware_flip.summary: Israeli restructuring relief can involve different ruling or statutory paths depending on whether the acquirer is public or private and on the transaction facts.
delaware_flip.applies_when: Use when estimating flip timing, tax deferral, or closing conditions.

date_window.notes: Apply law and ITA practice as of the proposed restructuring date.

warnings: Do not hardcode Section 104H as the only flip path.
Require Israeli tax counsel to select public-company, private-company, or alternate restructuring treatment.

delaware_flip.title: May 2025 Israeli restructuring changes
delaware_flip.summary: Secondary law-firm guidance reports that May 2025 Israeli restructuring amendments repealed restrictive Part E2 requirements, including certain holding-period and rights-continuity constraints.
delaware_flip.applies_when: Use when comparing pre- and post-May-2025 flip or restructuring assumptions.

date_window.notes: Effective month based on secondary law-firm summary; verify official legislation before implementation.

warnings: Do not apply old 25 percent/2-year continuity assumptions to post-amendment transactions without checking current law.

delaware_flip.title: Options, SAFEs, and notes in a flip
delaware_flip.summary: Options, SAFEs, and convertible notes require separate treatment in a flip, including trustee approvals, 102 continuity, holder consents, assignment, novation, and conversion-price preservation.
delaware_flip.applies_when: Use when a flip includes outstanding options, RSUs, SAFEs, convertible notes, or warrants.

date_window.notes: Check instrument terms and tax approvals as of closing.

warnings: Prompt for each instrument's assignment, amendment, and change-of-control provisions.
Escalate Israeli Section 102 continuity and trustee approvals.

delaware_flip.title: IIA-funded IP cannot be assumed transferable in a flip
delaware_flip.summary: IIA-funded technology may require approval or trigger repayment or licensing constraints before IP transfer, ownership migration, or manufacturing changes connected to a flip.
delaware_flip.applies_when: Use when an Israeli company with IIA-funded technology flips or reorganizes.
warnings: Flag IIA funding as a closing-condition and economics issue, not a cap-table-only detail.

delaware_flip.title: Flip timeline and cost are path-conditioned
delaware_flip.summary: Flip timing and cost depend on tax ruling path, consents, IIA history, instruments, holder mix, and counsel workflow; benchmarks should be low-confidence prompts, not script outputs.
delaware_flip.applies_when: Use only to explain why a flip estimate cannot be derived from cap-table math alone.

benchmark.notes: Use project-specific counsel estimates rather than generic public numbers.

warnings: Do not output a fixed flip cost or timeline without user-provided counsel estimate.

founder_benchmarks.title: Founder ownership stage medians
founder_benchmarks.summary: Carta founder-ownership datasets provide stage and IPO benchmarks for founder ownership, but they are observational benchmarks rather than fairness rules.
founder_benchmarks.applies_when: Use when comparing a founder's projected ownership to market benchmarks.

benchmark.use: Percentile or median comparison, never pass/fail scoring.

warnings: Do not treat a benchmark median as the correct ownership target.
Segment by stage, funding history, founder role, and company path when possible.

founder_benchmarks.title: No universal founder-ownership redlines
founder_benchmarks.summary: Founder ownership concerns are context-dependent; the skill should use configurable warnings and benchmark comparisons rather than universal claims such as a hard minimum after seed.
founder_benchmarks.applies_when: Use when evaluating dilution, stacked SAFEs, option-pool refreshes, or founder equity splits.
warnings: Warn on severe dilution using user-configurable thresholds and benchmark context.
Avoid categorical advice that a founder must retain a specific percentage.

founder_benchmarks.title: Israel pre-seed and seed context
founder_benchmarks.summary: Israel early-stage funding benchmarks should be kept separate from US benchmark datasets and treated as context for scenario ranges rather than cap-table rules.
founder_benchmarks.applies_when: Use when modeling Israeli pre-seed or seed scenarios.

benchmark.use: Scenario context by market and year; not a legal or valuation rule.

warnings: Do not mix Israel pre-seed benchmarks with US Carta founder-ownership medians without labeling the source market.

founder_benchmarks.title: Stacked SAFE dilution warning
founder_benchmarks.summary: Stacked SAFEs, pool top-ups, note conversions, and priced-round dilution can combine into unexpectedly large founder dilution; warnings should be based on scenario deltas and benchmark context.
founder_benchmarks.jurisdiction: US and Israel startup market; economics only
founder_benchmarks.applies_when: Use after running SAFE, note, option-pool, and financing conversion calculations.
warnings: Warn when founder ownership declines sharply between pre-financing and post-financing scenarios.
Show the drivers of dilution separately: SAFEs, notes, option pool, new-money shares, and anti-dilution.
